findings.finding: Air France-KLM's Q3 2026 release on 5 Nov beat consensus: adjusted operating profit EUR1,346m against about EUR1.1bn expected. North Atlantic yield rose 9.3% and the release says 'Demand in North America remained very solid'. Group unit revenue still slowed from +8.7% cc in Q2 to +7.0% cc in Q3, and Q4 booked load factor is about 1pt below 2025. IAG rose only +0.7% on the day while AF rose +15%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus (EUR1.41bn vs EUR1.37bn) and the stock fell 1.53%. Q3 2025 missed company consensus by 2% and fell 11.6%. The reported quarter has never been enough on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. IAG closed 5 Nov intraday at 439.4p (+0.7%), while AF.PA rose +14.8% and LHA +1.9% (Yahoo chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/IAG.L?range=1mo&interval=1d). If the market had carried the AF beat across to IAG, IAG would have moved with the sector on the day; it did not, and BofA's IAG model still assumes PRASK of only +4%. Against that, IAG had already rallied about 9% from 30 Oct, and AF's own gain is inflated by AF-specific short covering. This is a peer proxy, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: BofA expects IAG's Q3 EBIT 2% above consensus on 'solid' Atlantic demand and higher US fares (https://es.finance.yahoo.com/noticias/bank-of-america-prev%C3%A9-ebit-103120740.html)

findings.finding: IAG's FY26 fuel scenario of EUR8.3-8.6bn was set on the 27 July curve, when Brent was about $90. Brent then ran to $104-118 through September and October before falling to about $97 this week, and Air France-KLM raised its own FY fuel bill by $300m on 5 Nov. A higher IAG fuel scenario is therefore likely, against FY EBIT consensus of EUR4.37bn that already sits near the bottom of the 12-15% margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 31 Jul 2026 IAG cut capacity to flat and set the fuel scenario; the stock fell 1.53%. On 7 Nov 2025 an unchanged guide disappointed investors hoping for an upgrade (Goodbody via Dow Jones, https://www.itiger.com/news/2581711003) and the stock fell 11.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The oil path is public, and the stock's 7% five-day rally is the market pricing this week's oil fall. A raised fuel scenario is the arithmetic consequence of September and October actuals already being spent at higher prices, which this week's fall cannot undo. If the market had priced a fuel-led trim, consensus would have moved below the EUR4.37bn of 13 Oct and the stock would not be at its highest since September. Macro-to-company transmission with about 74% hedged, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: Brent weekly series (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BZ=F?range=6mo&interval=1wk); Air France-KLM's FY fuel bill raised from $8.9bn to $9.2bn (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/05/3396062/0/en/air-france-klm-q3-2026-results.html)

findings.finding: UBS capacity data, relayed on 4 Nov, has IAG cutting short-haul capacity in 2026 while Ryanair, Lufthansa and easyJet add seats, and limits IAG's long-haul growth to 0.4%. That supports IAG's yields relative to peers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The capacity cut to flat on 31 Jul 2026 coincided with a -1.53% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Capacity discipline is broadly known, because IAG guided flat capacity in July. What is less priced is the comparison with rivals who are adding seats. The source is secondary (UBS via Proactive via ad-hoc-news) and Proactive itself is unreachable, so it is kept small.

findings.finding: The interim dividend comes with the Q3 results under IAG's stated policy of paying about 50% of the annual dividend as an interim after Q3, with the total rising with inflation. The 2025 interim was EUR0.048 gross, declared 6 Nov 2025.

findings.why_not_priced: It is guided and small, at about 1% of the share price. The only open question is the size against an inflation-linked expectation, so it stays near 0.

findings.finding: The reaction function: IAG fell on each of its last five results days (-1.7%, -11.6%, -3.6%, -3.2%, -1.5%). In Nov 2025 an in-line quarter with an unchanged guide was sold because investors wanted an upgrade. This print arrives after a +7.2% five-day and +9% run from the 30 Oct close, and the stock sits just below the 449-451p resistance zone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of 5 results days were down, with a median of -3.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Here the run-up IS the price: the stock now carries the oil fall and the peer rally, so a reiterated 12-15% guide looks like the setup that was sold last year. If the market expected a disappointment, the stock would not have made a two-month high into the print.
findings.independence: Baseline reaction history from Investegate (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/IAG); IG preview on resistance levels (https://www.ig.com/uk/news-and-trade-ideas/iag-q3-results-preview-can-british-airways-owner-weather-the-fuel-cost-squeeze-261105)
